newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOVT SAYS MAY STEP IN TO FURTHER BLACK MINING ROLE.
newsitem.headline: GOVT SAYS MAY STEP IN TO FURTHER BLACK MINING ROLE.

text.p: South Africa's Mineral and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna said on Wednesday black involvement in the country's mining industry remained inadequate and government might use its muscle to facilitate the process.
Addressing the Investing in African Mining Conference he said that despite the recent purchase by a black consortium of a stake in mining house JCI Ltd , empowerment was proceeding slowly.
"After five years of political change in this country, there is still inadequate black participation at either an ownership or operational level," Maduna told delegates.
"The JCI deal is the most important, and even that has come very late in the day."
He said government was looking at an acceleration of black participation in the mining industry and would like to see this happen spontaneously and with the cooperation of mining firms.
"Lack of progress in this respect will leave us no option but to assist this process through appropriate mineral rights policies," Maduna said.

He gave no details of what such policies, on which a discussion document is due to be released soon, might dictate but said the lack of available mineral rights topped government's list of priorities.
Maduna said government would like to encourage the development of partnerships between black business interests and resourced mineral investors.
"This killing of two birds with one stone, as it were, would be a marvelous catalyst to restructuring and revitalising our industry."

In November last year Maduna said government was actively considering ways in which South Africa's unused mineral rights, held by both government and the private sector, could be used to create jobs and increase black ownership.
At the time he said the state did not have money to buy mineral rights from private companies and also ruled out nationalisation as an option.

The African Mining Group, a black grouping led by Capital Alliance Ltd , in November agreed to buy Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's 34.9 percent stake in JCI for 2.88 billion rand or 54.50 rand per share. The deadline to raise the necessary funds is February 28.

In January a key player, Thebe Investments Corp, announced it had pulled out of the consortium. Captall, however, said at the time it remained confident that the purchase would go ahead. JCI is South Africa's sixth largest mining house and the fourth largest gold producer.
